question: To roughly what fraction of its original volume does a diesel compress the fuel and air mixture, and how does that compare with a gasoline engine?
note: about one-twentieth in a diesel versus about one-eighth in a gasoline engine

question: Why does a diesel engine need no ignition system?
note: the mixture is ignited by the heat generated by compression, hence compression ignition

question: Why is a diesel engine difficult to start in cold weather?
note: diesel fuel is not very volatile

question: Why must a diesel engine be built much heavier than a gasoline engine?
note: it needs the strength to deal with the tighter compression of the mixture

question: What property of diesel fuel makes it less likely to explode in a collision?
note: it is oily in consistency and less volatile than gasoline

question: Why does a two-stroke cycle diesel require a supercharger?
note: piston movement alone will not force in intake air and push out exhaust gases

question: In a two-stroke cycle diesel, where are the exhaust valves and where are the intake ports located?
note: exhaust valve on top of the combustion chamber; intake ports cut into the cylinder wall

question: In a two-stroke cycle gasoline engine, why is the top of the piston shaped rather than flat?
note: to divert the incoming mixture upward and away from the exhaust port

question: A two-stroke engine fires every revolution, so why does it not produce twice the power of an equivalent four-stroke?
note: stated as a disadvantage; scavenging is imperfect and the supercharger consumes engine power

question: Why is a vehicle horn normally operated through a relay rather than wired straight to its switch?
note: the current draw of a horn is very high

question: How are the tone and volume of a horn adjusted?
note: loosen the adjusting locknut and turn the adjusting nut, which controls the current consumed

question: What happens to a horn if too much current is supplied to it?
note: it will sputter and may lock the diaphragm

question: In a dual horn installation, what controls the sound frequency of the low-pitch horn?
note: a long air column

question: Why do vacuum-operated windshield wipers slow down or stop when a vehicle climbs a hill?
note: they run on intake manifold vacuum, and manifold pressure varies with engine loading

question: What drawback did early electric windshield wipers have, and what change removed it?
note: heavy current demand on 6-volt systems; solved when 12-volt systems became standard

question: What is the purpose of the park switch built into a windshield wiper motor?
note: it keeps the motor powered long enough to return the arms and blades to a retracted position after switch-off

question: On which vehicles are air-operated windshield wipers used almost exclusively?
note: heavy vehicles equipped with airbrakes

question: How is the rotary output of an electric wiper motor turned into the back-and-forth motion of the wiper arms?
note: a worm gear drives a shaft connected to a crank, and the wiper transmission converts the circular motion to reciprocating motion

question: Where on the vehicle is the auxiliary power receptacle usually installed?
note: at the right-rear corner of the cab body, near the vehicle batteries

question: Why does the auxiliary power receptacle simplify charging the batteries from an external source?
note: you unscrew the cap and plug in the connector; no disconnecting and reconnecting of battery cables

question: What openings does the heater unit box contain?
note: outside air intake, interior air intake, defroster outlets, heater outlets and ventilation outlets

question: What actuates a backup alarm on a large vehicle?
note: shifting the transmission into reverse

question: Why is a torque converter, rather than a driver-operated clutch, used to couple an automatic transmission to the engine?
note: it does not have to be manually disengaged every time the vehicle stops, and its fluid coupling cushions the drive

question: Which three signals does the valve body of an automatic transmission act on?
note: vehicle speed, throttle position and gearshift lever position

question: What is the purpose of the pressure plates in an automatic transmission's multiple-disk clutch?
note: they distribute the application pressure equally over the clutch disks and plates

question: What prevents hydraulic pressure leaking around the clutch piston in an automatic transmission?
note: clutch piston seals on the inner and outer circumferences

question: What is an automatic transmission brake band made from, and how is its inner surface finished?
note: a circular piece of spring steel, rectangular in cross section, lined on its inside circumference with friction material

question: What approximate speed reduction ratio does the compound planetary drive train give in low gear?
note: about 1.8 to 1

question: Up to roughly what road speed does a Simpson drive train stay in low with the lever in drive?
note: from zero to approximately eight miles per hour

question: Why has the compound planetary drive train largely replaced designs using two separate planetary gearsets?
note: its compactness, achieved by integrating two gearsets through long and short pinions

question: Why does an automatic transmission transmit no torque when the lever is in neutral?
note: clutches and brake bands are released, so there is no reactionary member in the planetary gearset to provide positive drive

question: Why does an automatic transmission's hydraulic system route oil through a remote cooler?
note: to remove excess heat generated in the transmission and torque converter

question: Besides planetary gearing, what mechanisms are contained within a cross-drive transmission?
note: the steering mechanism, the braking mechanism and hydraulically operated clutches, driven through a torque converter

question: In what driving conditions would the driver of a tracked vehicle select low range on a cross-drive transmission?
note: when extra driving torque is needed, for instance pulling through heavy mud or sand

question: What changes in the power path when the lockup clutch in the torque converter engages?
note: pump and turbine are locked together and turn as a unit, so no hydraulic torque conversion occurs and drive becomes direct mechanical

question: When a tracked vehicle is driving straight ahead, how much power passes through the steering system of a cross-drive transmission?
note: none, because neither steer clutch is engaged while both output flanges turn at the same speed and direction

question: During a steer in neutral range, why do the output ring gears stay stationary while the sun gears turn in opposite directions?
note: both ring gears are splined to the cross-drive shaft, so they cannot rotate in opposite directions

question: Do the hydraulic system and the lubrication system of a cross-drive transmission use separate oil supplies?
note: no, the hydraulic system and the lubrication system operate from the same oil

question: What is the torque specification, in pound-feet, for the cross-drive transmission output flange retaining bolts?
note: a principles manual; carries no torque values

question: How many quarts of oil does the cross-drive transmission hold at a dry fill?
note: no fluid capacities are given anywhere in this manual

question: At what mileage interval should windshield wiper blades be replaced?
note: no service or replacement intervals are given

question: What is the national stock number for the horn relay?
note: part numbering lives in the parts catalogue, not the principles manual

question: What amperage fuse protects the horn circuit?
note: the horn relay and its high current draw are described, but no fuse rating is given

question: What wire gauge is specified for the cables running to the auxiliary power receptacle?
note: the receptacle is described but no conductor sizing is specified

question: Which viscosity grade of automatic transmission fluid should be used in the Simpson drive train?
note: no lubricant grades or specifications are given

question: What is the diagnostic procedure when an automatic transmission slips on the one-to-two upshift?
note: the manual explains operating principles; it contains no troubleshooting procedures

question: Which vehicle model years were fitted with the Simpson drive train?
note: the drive train is described generically, with no model or year applicability list

question: What is the maximum allowable brake band lining wear before the band must be replaced?
note: band construction is described but no wear limits are given

question: How many turns of the horn adjusting nut correspond to a one-ampere change in current draw?
note: the adjustment is described qualitatively as very sensitive, with no calibration figure

question: Which manufacturer supplies the cross-drive transmissions described in this manual?
note: several models are referred to generically; no manufacturer is named

question: What cold-cranking amperage is required to start a diesel engine at minus twenty degrees Fahrenheit?
note: cold starting difficulty is explained qualitatively, with no electrical requirement given

question: What track tension, in inches of sag, should be set on a vehicle using a cross-drive transmission?
note: the transmission drives the tracks but no track adjustment specification appears

question: What is the pin assignment of the connector on the windshield wiper park switch?
note: the park switch function is described; no wiring pinout is provided

question: How long, in hours, does a complete cross-drive transmission overhaul take?
note: no labour or maintenance time standards appear in this manual
